summary: Fludarabine phosphate is an intravenous purine-analog antimetabolite indicated for adult B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) that has not responded to or has progressed during at least one alkylating-agent regimen. It carries a BOXED WARNING: it can cause severe bone marrow suppression; at high doses (about 4 times the CLL dose) it caused dose-dependent severe CNS toxicity including delayed blindness, coma, and death, and similar severe neurotoxicity has occurred at recommended doses; life-threatening, sometimes fatal autoimmune hemolytic anemia and other autoimmune phenomena can occur after one or more cycles; and combination with pentostatin caused an unacceptably high incidence of fatal pulmonary toxicity. It must NOT be combined with pentostatin. Tumor lysis syndrome, serious/opportunistic infections, and transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease are additional hazards. The recommended dose is 25 mg/m2 IV daily for 5 days every 28 days, reduced in renal impairment.
indications: Treatment of adult patients with B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) who have not responded to or whose disease has progressed during treatment with at least one standard alkylating-agent containing regimen

moa: Fludarabine phosphate is rapidly dephosphorylated to 2-fluoro-ara-A and then phosphorylated intracellularly by deoxycytidine kinase to the active triphosphate 2-fluoro-ara-ATP. This metabolite inhibits DNA polymerase alpha, ribonucleotide reductase, and DNA primase, thereby inhibiting DNA synthesis. The full mechanism of this antimetabolite is not completely characterized and may be multi-faceted.

absolute: Combination with pentostatin (deoxycoformycin) - unacceptably high incidence of fatal pulmonary toxicity
Severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance less than 30 mL/min) - do not administer
relative: Pre-existing bone marrow impairment or cytopenias
Moderate renal impairment (CrCl 30-79 mL/min) - reduce dose and monitor closely
Prior or active autoimmune hemolytic anemia / positive Coombs test
High tumor burden / risk of tumor lysis syndrome
monitor: Signs of hemolysis (hemoglobin, Coombs test, reticulocytes, bilirubin)
Signs of infection and tumor lysis syndrome

preg: Based on its mechanism of action, fludarabine phosphate can cause fetal harm; there are no adequate well-controlled studies in pregnant women. It was embryolethal and teratogenic in rats and rabbits (cleft palate, hydrocephaly, skeletal/visceral malformations, increased resorptions). Women of childbearing potential should avoid becoming pregnant; if used during pregnancy, advise the patient of the potential hazard to the fetus. Males with female partners of childbearing potential should use contraception during and after therapy.
lact: It is not known whether fludarabine phosphate is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions including tumorigenicity in nursing infants, decide whether to discontinue nursing or discontinue the drug, taking into account the importance of the drug to the mother.
renal: Renal excretion of the active metabolite 2-fluoro-ara-A is significant (about 40% of total clearance). Reduce the starting dose for creatinine clearance 30-79 mL/min (20 mg/m2 for 50-79 mL/min; 15 mg/m2 for 30-49 mL/min) and monitor closely for excessive toxicity. Do not administer if creatinine clearance is less than 30 mL/min.
hepatic: The label does not define a specific hepatic dose adjustment. Use with caution; debilitated patients should be monitored closely for excessive toxicity.

major: Pentostatin (deoxycoformycin) - CONTRAINDICATED combination; unacceptably high incidence of fatal pulmonary toxicity. Do NOT co-administer.
Non-irradiated blood products - risk of fatal transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease; use only irradiated blood
Alkylating agents, topoisomerase inhibitors, or irradiation (prior/concomitant/subsequent) - associated with reported myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukemia
moderate: Other myelosuppressive chemotherapy - additive bone marrow suppression
Live vaccines - avoid in immunosuppressed patients
Immunosuppressants - additive immunosuppression and infection risk
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described; supportive care and adequate hydration are advised given toxicity profile.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause elevations of pancreatic enzyme levels; positive direct antiglobulin (Coombs) test may accompany autoimmune hemolysis.

Serious and opportunistic infections (including reactivation of VZV, EBV)
Pneumonia and pulmonary hypersensitivity (dyspnea, cough, interstitial infiltrates)

BOXED WARNING - life-threatening/fatal autoimmune hemolytic anemia, immune thrombocytopenia, Evans syndrome, acquired hemophilia
BOXED WARNING - fatal pulmonary toxicity (especially with pentostatin); ARDS, pulmonary hemorrhage, respiratory failure

monitoring: CBC with differential before and frequently during treatment (anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia)
Signs of hemolysis - hemoglobin, reticulocytes, bilirubin, direct Coombs test (discontinue if hemolysis occurs)
Neurologic assessment - vision, mental status, seizures, weakness
Signs and symptoms of infection (including opportunistic/viral)
Tumor lysis labs in high-risk patients - uric acid, potassium, phosphate, calcium, renal function
Renal function (creatinine clearance) to guide dosing
counsel: This is a strong chemotherapy medicine given by vein; you will be watched closely for low blood counts and infection
Report any vision changes, confusion, severe weakness, or seizures immediately - these can be serious nervous-system effects
Report unusual tiredness, dark urine, yellowing, or rapid heartbeat - signs of red-cell breakdown (hemolysis)
Report fever, chills, cough, or trouble breathing right away
If you need a blood transfusion, tell the team you are on this drug so irradiated blood is used
Avoid pregnancy; use effective contraception (both men and women) during and after treatment
This drug must never be combined with pentostatin
pk: Rapidly converted to active 2-fluoro-ara-A within minutes of IV infusion
Maximum 2-fluoro-ara-A at end of infusion; moderate accumulation over the 5-day course
Dosed daily x5 every 28 days; plasma trough roughly doubles over the 5-day schedule
Store refrigerated at 2 to 8 C (36 to 46 F); use reconstituted/opened solution within 8 hours
pearls: BOXED WARNING: severe bone marrow suppression; dose-dependent severe CNS toxicity (delayed blindness, coma, death) at high doses and rarely at recommended doses; life-threatening autoimmune hemolytic anemia; and fatal pulmonary toxicity
NEVER combine with pentostatin (deoxycoformycin) - the combination caused an unacceptably high rate of FATAL pulmonary toxicity and is not recommended
Always use irradiated blood products to prevent fatal transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease
Discontinue if autoimmune hemolysis develops; most patients rechallenged have recurrence of hemolysis
Reduce dose for CrCl 30-79 mL/min and do not give below 30 mL/min - renal excretion is a major elimination pathway
Take precautions for tumor lysis syndrome in high-burden disease; monitor for opportunistic infection and PML
missed: Not self-administered. Doses are given as a clinician-administered 5-day IV course every 28 days; a delayed or missed dose is managed by the oncology team, who may delay or reduce dosing based on blood counts and toxicity. Patients should keep all scheduled appointments.
overdose: High doses have caused irreversible CNS toxicity (delayed blindness, coma, death) and severe thrombocytopenia and neutropenia from bone marrow suppression. There is no specific antidote. Treatment is drug discontinuation and supportive care.
